name: GET /api/leadflow/checkout/:id/status - the assistance signal
description:
Reports a checkout's state, and flags STARTED-BUT-NOT-PAID as the highest priority signal on the screen (db21f0db-8754-4be1-b3db-d367fff9af12#AC4). Somebody reached for their card and something stopped them - a declined card, a confusing field, a second thought. It is the most recoverable moment in the whole funnel and the shortest-lived, which is why it outranks every other task rather than joining the queue.

A FAILED CHECKOUT CARRIES THE SAME PRIORITY. From the buyer's side the experience is identical: they tried to pay and did not end up a customer.

PENDING OR FAILED NEVER ADVANCES THE STAGE (db21f0db-8754-4be1-b3db-d367fff9af12#AC3). may_close_won is true only for a checkout the gateway confirmed as paid, and the rule is restated in the response because the screen that shows a started checkout is exactly where somebody is tempted to mark the deal won early.

QA: reads the checkout created earlier in the chain from the cache. A freshly sent checkout is 'sent', so may_close_won is false and priority is normal - which is the AC3 assertion.

testCases.name: A sent-but-unpaid checkout does not permit Closed Won
NEGATIVE: no checkout with that id
NEGATIVE: no Authorization header at all
NEGATIVE: a bearer token that does not verify

errorCases.when: the checkout id does not exist.

errorCases.message: Authorization header with a bearer token is required
errorCases.when: the Authorization header is absent, empty, or uses a scheme other than Bearer.

errorCases.message: Session token is invalid or expired
errorCases.when: a Bearer token was presented but does not verify.
